issues.description: Close message sends {"type":"Close"} but Deepgram's documented contract is {"type":"CloseStream"}
issues.detail: PR description and Deepgram docs specify CloseStream as the control message, but _CLOSE_MSG sends Close. Either the wire string is wrong or the description is wrong. If Deepgram silently ignores unknown types, the graceful-shutdown contract is broken without any signal to callers. Fix the constant to match the documented protocol.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout does not actually drain remaining audio frames
issues.detail: Sending Flush+Close then reading exactly one frame is a guess, not a handshake. The implied postcondition is that remaining TTS audio is received before close, but one receive() captures at most one frame. Either loop until a terminal/ack message or until the server closes, using the timeout as an overall budget.

issues.description: Bare 'except Exception' hides protocol errors and unspecified _close_ws preconditions
issues.detail: _close_ws now runs in success, error, and already-closed paths without stating its precondition. The broad except around send_str/receive collapses connection errors, protocol bugs, and benign closed-socket cases into identical warnings. Narrow to ConnectionError/WebSocketError, check ws.closed before send, or mirror STT's existing handling.

issues.description: Control-message constants should be shared with STT, not duplicated per class
issues.detail: STT already defines a CloseStream control message; TTS now defines its own _FLUSH_MSG and _CLOSE_MSG. The Deepgram wire protocol is one ADT — centralize these constants in a shared protocol module so STT and TTS cannot drift silently. Two copies of the same protocol string is exactly the duplication that caused this bug.

issues.description: Flush-on-close is a separate behavior change bundled into a Close-message bugfix
issues.detail: The PR is titled and described as a CloseStream fix, but it also unconditionally sends Flush on every close. That is an independent behavior change with its own justification and should be a separate commit. Bundling silently smuggles in semantics under an unrelated title.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the headline issue is a contract mismatch: the code sends {"type":"Close"} while the PR description and Deepgram docs specify {"type":"CloseStream"}. The new _close_ws also fails to actually drain remaining audio — a single receive() with a 1s timeout is not a real handshake — and the broad except hides whether the close postcondition held. Control-message constants are duplicated rather than shared with STT, and a Flush-on-close behavior change is smuggled into a bugfix. Fix the wire string, drain properly, narrow the exception, centralize the protocol constants, and split the Flush change before merge.
